{
  "winner": "B",
  "reasons": [
    "The goal is one paying customer within 90 days. B sells through self-serve Shopify App Store installs with monthly card billing, and paid App Store ads can start at $5/day. A's own brief says municipal procurement (RFPs, insurance certificates, cooperative-purchasing vetting) is slow and bureaucratic, which conflicts directly with a 90-day window.",
    "B's competitors show that small merchants pay for this category at $5–$130/month. AltText.ai has 141 reviews at 4.5 stars, which is a sign of a working paid market. B also identifies a gap the free Shopify Magic does not fill: alt text, images, titles and bulk editing. That gives a solo builder a concrete wedge.",
    "B's technical pattern (vision LLM plus Admin API write-back) is proven by several live apps and can be automated end to end with agents. A's defensible layer, legally reliable compliance documentation, carries liability that the brief says a solo, uninsured operator is poorly placed to absorb.",
    "A's acquisition channels are weak for a fast start. The booth pricing comes from a 2015 prospectus, the state-league booths cited are already sold out, and the free-audit funnel copies what GovAccess and CASO Comply already run.",
    "B's risks are real: saturation, possible one-time-per-catalog churn, and demand evidence made of three Reddit quotes with no payment signal. However, these risks mainly threaten long-term retention and scale, not the narrower goal of landing a first paying customer."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "A's demand evidence rests on two quotes from one news article about a single county (Cole County, MO). One of them, Landwehr's, describes complying by removing information from the website rather than buying a tool. That points away from willingness to pay, not toward it.",
  "confidence_note": "Moderate confidence. A has stronger evidence of real money spent ($7,000 in Cole County, a $2,510 quote to Templeton) and a hard regulatory deadline, so it may be the better business over a longer horizon. B wins mainly because the 90-day, solo-operator constraint favors self-serve distribution over municipal procurement. B's demand evidence is anecdotal, and its ADA settlement figures come from vendor blogs."
}
